newsitem.title: CANADA: New Canada poll suggests slim Liberal majority.
newsitem.headline: New Canada poll suggests slim Liberal majority.

text.p: Canada's ruling Liberals are set to win the June 2 federal election with a slim majority, according to a poll released on Tuesday.

The survey of 3,000 voters from May 22-25 showed that 37.8 percent of decided voters intended to vote Liberal. The Conservatives had 21.2 percent support, the Reform Party 17.7 percent, the New Democratic Party 11.3 percent and the separatist Bloc Quebecois 9.7 percent.
The poll was done by Ekos Research Associates, with a margin of error of plus or minus 1.8 percent, 19 times out of 20. One-third of the sample was from Quebec.
The survey showed Liberal strength in Ontario, with favorable splits in the rest of the country that would likely yield a bare Liberal majority.
"This could well become a minority with any further erosion, although there appears to be little turbulence and little underlying reason to expect much," the pollsters said.
They predicted the right-wing Reform Party was poised to form the official opposition, despite less popular support than the Tories.
The poll showed that 27.6 percent of respondents were undecided.

The poll numbers were in line with results from a Reuters-Zogby daily tracking poll. Results from the rolling poll on Monday showed the Liberals with 42.2 percent, the Conservatives 20.6 percent, Reform 19.3 percent, the NDP 9.9 percent and the Bloc 6.3 percent. A total of 32.6 percent were undecided.
The Reuters-Zogby poll surveyed 1.014 voters with a margin of error of 3.2 percentage points.
The rolling poll is to be updated later on Tuesday.
